sentences.text: At the outset learned counsel for the appellant submits that he does not want to press I.A.No.9877/2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant-Narayan and insists for final hearing of this appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: There is no opposition to such prayer by the learned Government Advocate.

sentences.text: With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, appeal is heard finally.

sentences.text:
2. This appeal is filed by the appellant/accused being aggrieved of the judgment dated 11.1.2025 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act), Khandwa in SC ATR No.99/2022 [State of M.P.
through P.S.Chhaigaonmakhan Vs. Narayan] whereby the appellant has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 2 CRA-1743-2025 convicted under sections 376(2)(N), 376(3) of IPC &
sections 5(L) r/w 6 of the POCSO Act and section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and acquitted from charges u/s 363, 366 & 376 ('Gha') of IPC and he has been sentenced as under:-
In Fine default Sentence Imprisonment Amount of fine amount Rs.2,000/-

sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In short, prosecution story is that on 02.6.2022 in morning at about 11.00 am mother of the prosecutrix had gone for working as a labourer and when she returned from work, prosecutrix was not found at home.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: She made search for prosecutrix and accordingly First Information Report (Ex.P/11) Crime No.257/2022 was registered under section 363 IPC and Missing Person Report (Exhibit-P/10) was lodged.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The case was investigated, in which, proof of age from the school record was obtained.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: When prosecutrix was recovered she was medically examined.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Her statements were recorded.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: After completing the other formalities charge-sheet was filed.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Accused denied the charges.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: After evidence of prosecution witnesses, when accused was confronted with the prosecution evidence he again stated that he is innocent but did not lead any defence evidence in the trial Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. This appeal has been filed on the ground that there are serious contradictions and omissions in the prosecution case.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is not proved that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, prayer has been made to allow the instant appeal and acquit the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate supported the judgment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 3 CRA-1743-2025 of the trial Court and submitted that it is well founded and same does not call for any interference by this Court on any ground.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. We have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
7. PW.1 (Kaluram) Headmaster of the School has stated that as per School Register (Exhibit-P/4)
the date of birth of prosecutrix is recorded as 19.8.2007.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 4 of the cross-examination he stated that at the time of admission in school the date of birth certificate was not produced.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
On his own he stated that date of birth is provided by 'Aganwadi' but in Exhibit-P/4 (Scholar Register)
there is no note or document to this effect that any information regarding date of birth was received from 'Aganwadi'.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 6 he further stated that on Exhibit- P/5 (Progress Report) the first date of birth, which was mentioned, was informed on estimation.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. PW.2 (prosecutrix) stated that she is 15 years of age and the incident is of six months ago.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 5 of her cross-examination she stated that her date of birth is not recorded with her father and mother.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: She also admitted that no proper birth certificate is issued by the Government to any member of the family.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 6 she stated that her current age is 22 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded on 17.11.2022 and offence is of 02.6.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In cross- examination she stated that before the incident she was married and had lived in a matrimonial home for about 08 months and then she came back.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: She got married, when she was 18 years of age.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. PW.3 (mother of the Prosecutrix) has stated in her examination-in-chief that prosecutrix is 15 years of age.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 5 of her cross-examination she stated that she does not remember the date of birth of prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 10 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 4 CRA-1743-2025 of her cross-examination she admitted that when she went to school to get children admitted then she had asked the Teacher to record the date of birth on his own estimation, looking to the height and health of children.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 11 she stated that in School, Court and to the Police she has narrated the age of the prosecutrix by estimation.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
11. In view of above, when we appreciate the oral and documentary evidence on record we find that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of offence prosecutrix was less than 18 years,
especially in the light of statements of the prosecutrix (PW.2) made in paragraph 6 and that of her mother (PW.3) in paragraphs 5, 10 & 11.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the finding of the learned trial Court regarding age of the prosecutrix in paragraph 34 is set aside.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, it is held that on the date of offence prosecutrix is not proved to be minor, being less than 18 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 12. Prosecutrix (PW.2) in paragraph 1 has stated that inspite of her objecting that she would go with the accused he took her on motorcycle to the house of Rohan and then he raped her many times.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: She further stated that when appellant/Narayan went out of the room, thereafter Rohan came and he also raped her thrice.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Both of them raped her multiple times.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 10 of her cross- examination she stated that on the date of incident appellant/Narayan did not do any wrong with her.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, she went to her sister's house so as to her mother think as if she had gone to her sister's (Aarti) house.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In Aarti's house she had changed her clothes and had washed herself.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 11 she stated that her mother assaulted her and lodged report against appellant/accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 12 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 5 CRA-1743-2025 she stated that in school her date of birth was recorded on estimation looking to her height and health.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In paragraph 12 she stated that out of pressure of her mother she state to the Police and before Court regarding rape.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Appellant- Narayan has not done any wrong with her.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, on re-examination by the prosecution as to whether appellant has raped her or not she has given contradictory statements in examination-in-chief and in cross-examination.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: She stated that whatever she has stated in examination-in-chief is correct, and whatever she deposed in cross-examination is wrong.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is worthwhile to note here that entire statements of the prosecutrix including examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination was recorded on the same date.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In re- examination by the defence in paragraph 13, this witness again stated that she is stating about rape out of pressure of her mother, who is sitting in Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 13. PW.7 (Dr.Ruplata Patel) has stated that on medical examination of the prosecutrix she did not found any injury on her body.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Her hymen was torn.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 14. Therefore, looking to the medical evidence, as deposed by the Lady Doctor, and looking to the evidence of Prosecutrix (PW.2), who changed her version on the same date at a short intervals, as to whether appellant/accused did wrong with the prosecutrix and if any relationship was made whether the same was made against her will or with her consent, we find that her statements were changing frequently and the same cannot be relied upon, therefore, it cannot be said that the relationship which was made by her and is supported by DNA report (Ex.P/27), was against her consent.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 15. Accordingly, appeal is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Impugned judgment of conviction and sentence by the trial Court is set aside.

Author: Vivek Rusia
Bench: Vivek Rusia
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

 (Narayan Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh 
 Dated : 10-01-2025
 Mr. Nilesh Dave, counsel for the appellant.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__decision:
For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed.
The appeal is admitted for final hearing.
This appeal is of the year 2022 and the final hearing of this appeal would take long time to conclude.
Hence the remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended.
Accordingly, IA No.18330/2024 stands allowed.
The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant Narayan S/o Shri Kanhaiyalal @ Kaniram Mali is hereby suspended and it is ordered that the appellant No.1 be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of trial court and subject to depositing of the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 14.05.2025 and also on such further dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
List the appeal for final hearing in due course.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__facts:
The appellant - Narayan has been convicted for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(M) of IPC, 1860 and Sections 3(1)(w-i), 3(1)(w-ii) & 3(2)
(v) of SC/ST (PA) Act, 1989 and sentenced to undergo RI of 10 years and 02 years each and Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.2000/-, Rs.1000/- and Rs.500/- each with further default stipulation.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__arguments:
Counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the aforesaid offence.
He further submits that he filed the application after completion of five years of jail sentence of present appellant.
Per contra, counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application and prays for 2 CRA-8253-2022 its rejection.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__ANALYSIS: Taking into consideration the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the custody period of appellant as well as record, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence and grant the benefit of suspension to appellant.

opennyai_summary.10_March_2025__arguments:
He further submits that during the pendency of the trial, appellant made an application to produce the CCTV footage of the bus stand where the incident is alleged to have taken place, but the same was not produced stating that there there was no CCTV camera.
However, in another case, the same Investigating Officer has filed the CCTV footage.
Further, Rakesh (DW-1) who is the owner of a shop in the bus stand, was a prosecution witness whose statement was recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C. but was not produced before the Court, hence, the appellant produced DW-1 as a defence witness.
There is no DNA report in the case.
Appellant has undergone 7 years of jail sentence.
Appeal is of the year 2018 and its final disposal will take considerable time.
Hence, in such circumstances, prayer is made for suspension of the jail sentence and grant of bail.
opennyai_summary.10_March_2025__ANALYSIS: 05. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that the application for suspension of custodial sentence filed on behalf of the appellant deserves to be allowed.
